name: Samut
description: A renowned initiate, master of the double khopesh and a dependable leader among her crop; she later became a planeswalker.

timeline.summary: Meris names the lost dissenter Samut, angering Djeru, who explains she chose heresy and was removed; Gideon recalls seeing a woman shouting that the gods lie.
timeline.quote: She is a dissenter ,

timeline.summary: On the eve of their Harvest, Samut finds Nakht by the river and the friends play-fight, joined by Djeru.
timeline.quote: Samut gave him a playful shove, sending him stumbling back into the water

timeline.summary: Nakht confesses his fears that the three will be separated and that his faith may falter; Samut says that questions are part of faith.
timeline.quote: What if my faith falters?

timeline.summary: The trio sneaks out of the Children's Quarters at night, and Nakht reveals he can command water.
timeline.quote: a small gush of water swirled sprang from the fountain and danced around his fingertips.

timeline.summary: Samut leads her friends to an old mural of Hazoret and strange fighting forms, which she performs.
timeline.quote: Samut assumed the first stance on the mural

timeline.summary: Nakht wonders aloud whether there was a time before the gods, unsettling his friends.
timeline.quote: if there ever was a time before the gods.

timeline.summary: Djeru shows his secret, a hole in the Hekma, and Nakht persuades the others to go out and look for themselves.
timeline.quote: working his way through the near-invisible hole in the Hekma

timeline.summary: The three children crawl through the barrier into the desert wastes.
timeline.quote: then dropped to her belly and began crawling through to the other side.

timeline.summary: In the desert they find a half-buried statue and ruins, and a gigantic limbed thing in the distance sends them fleeing.
timeline.quote: a looming . . . thing shuffled across the sand.

timeline.summary: In a ruined shrine they find the word Trespasser freshly carved beneath the God-Pharaoh's symbol.
timeline.quote: Trespasser.

timeline.summary: Rotting corpses rise from the oasis and swarm the shrine, which Djeru calls dissenters returned by the curse of wandering.
timeline.quote: From the stagnant water and the surrounding sands, rotting corpses started to rise.

timeline.summary: Nakht draws the risen away and conjures a whirlpool to hold them while Samut and Djeru escape.
timeline.quote: The stagnant waters beneath him swirled into a whirlpool

timeline.summary: Samut sees Nakht wither to a lifeless husk, and Djeru tackles her out of sight; they flee back to the city at dawn.
timeline.quote: She heard his soul-rending screech as he instantly withered and decayed

timeline.summary: Years later, the loss hardens Djeru's faith while Samut takes up doubt and searches the ancient parts of Naktamun.
timeline.quote: took up the mantle of doubt and questions

timeline.summary: Samut finds a sealed chamber in Bontu's Monument and sees the God-Pharaoh named Trespasser.
timeline.quote: The walls of the shadowed chamber spoke of the God-Pharaoh's first arrival on Amonkhet

timeline.summary: Samut realizes that the God-Pharaoh is the Great Trespasser who caused the calamity rather than saving the plane, and resolves to warn everyone.
timeline.quote: He caused it.

timeline.summary: As Samut sprints from the chamber, dark magic flickers to life across the runes.
timeline.quote: a dark magic slowly flickered to life across the runes.

timeline.summary: Samut hides in an old embalming chamber after fleeing viziers and the anointed, and meets Djeru, who came disguised as a mummy.
timeline.quote: The wholesome face of her friend Djeru emerged

timeline.summary: Samut begs Djeru not to enter the final Trial, claiming the God-Pharaoh is a lie, but he refuses and walks out.
timeline.quote: Don't go to the final Trial.

timeline.summary: Samut mentions Nakht, and Djeru angrily says Nakht died unworthy because of their foolish trespass.
timeline.quote: Nakht died unworthy , out there in the dunes, because of our stupidity.

timeline.summary: Djeru leaves, saying he will plead to Hazoret for her, which gives Samut an idea.
timeline.quote: I'll plead to Hazoret for you.

timeline.summary: Samut enters Hazoret's monument and requests an audience with the god.
timeline.quote: I request an audience, mighty Hazoret.

timeline.summary: Samut asks Hazoret not to take Djeru's life, and Hazoret questions her right to cage his heart.
timeline.quote: I have come to plead for Djeru's survival.

timeline.summary: Samut dares to ask whether Hazoret herself is mistaken and appeals to the god of compassion she once was before the God-Pharaoh.
timeline.quote: Any tiny sliver of a memory of that time before the God-Pharaoh?

timeline.summary: Hazoret curses Samut and orders the anointed to seize the dissenter.
timeline.quote: Seize the dissenter.

timeline.summary: Samut is imprisoned in a sarcophagus among other dissenters, who tell her dissenters are the monsters of the Trial of Zeal.
timeline.quote: The monsters initiates face in the final Trial are the dissenters themselves.

timeline.summary: Samut explains that she needs to save Djeru, believing he could convince a god they were lied to.
timeline.quote: If anyone could convince a god they'd been lied to, it's him.

timeline.summary: Gideon and Chandra free Samut from the sarcophagus, telling her they came to rescue her.
timeline.quote: He explained that they saw her days ago evading capture and came to rescue her.

timeline.summary: The Gatewatch share information with Samut, learning that Bolas is a dragon from another world and has tampered with the gods.
timeline.quote: The God-Pharaoh is a dragon from another world, Samut.

timeline.summary: Samut forces the group to focus on rescuing Djeru, and Gideon swears to help.
timeline.quote: I swear to help you save the life of your friend.

timeline.summary: All the gods approach and Hazoret takes Samut and the Gatewatch to face the last initiates, knocking them out.
timeline.quote: Your time has come

timeline.summary: The dissidents awake in the arena with cartouches of control, and Nissa learns to move against the cartouche by treating it like a leyline.
timeline.quote: They work like leylines

timeline.summary: Hazoret orders the initiates to kill the heretics and starts the final Trial, casting her mark of battle rage over everyone.
timeline.quote: Hazoret's mark of battle rage appeared over their heads.

timeline.summary: The Gatewatch fight without magic, and Samut reaches Djeru and fights alongside him.
timeline.quote: She would protect him. They would fight together.

timeline.summary: Djeru prays for Samut's forgiveness while he and Samut fight, and he slices Gideon's arm.
timeline.quote: cutting a sleek, shallow slice cut through Gideon's forearm

timeline.summary: The battle magic fades, and Djeru surrenders his khopesh and prays for Samut's glorified death.
timeline.quote: Djeru concluded with his khopesh on the ground, a formal surrender.

timeline.summary: Hazoret asks Djeru to claim his place, and he accepts, but Samut declines Hazoret's gift.
timeline.quote: Without hesitation, she shook her head.

timeline.summary: As Hazoret strikes, Samut tackles Djeru out of the way and Gideon blocks the spear with his golden barrier.
timeline.quote: He stood between them and Hazoret's spear

timeline.summary: Djeru, enraged that his chance at a glorious death is gone, beats on Gideon and weeps that he wants to exist.
timeline.quote: Because I want to exist!

timeline.summary: The second sun passes through the horns, a shadow crosses the arena, and the Hours begin.
timeline.quote: It has begun. The Hours have begun!

timeline.summary: Djeru and Samut run to the Luxa as the Hours begin amid a stampede of citizens, and Hazoret strides to the river.
timeline.quote: all racing toward the banks of the Luxa River.

timeline.summary: Samut asks Djeru to promise to protect their gods and each other.
timeline.quote: No matter what happens, we protect our gods. We protect each other.

timeline.summary: The second sun reaches its final point and the Gate cracks open, then swings wide to reveal endless wastes instead of paradise.
timeline.quote: What lay beyond the Gate were endless, empty wastes.

timeline.summary: Samut asks Hazoret if that is paradise, and the god does not answer.
timeline.quote: Is that paradise?

timeline.summary: A winged demon flies through the Gate and perches on an obelisk, and Samut recognizes it.
timeline.quote: Demons were rare on Amonkhet.

timeline.summary: Samut asks Djeru whether he still believes the God-Pharaoh is benevolent, and Djeru's doubt grows.
timeline.quote: Do you still believe this is the act of a benevolent God-Pharaoh?

timeline.summary: Hapatra takes Samut and Djeru onto Tuya as they seek to protect Oketra.
timeline.quote: The two former initiates gracefully climbed atop Tuya

timeline.summary: Hapatra weeps for her gods, then tells Gideon the source of the hell is his responsibility to kill.
timeline.quote: Then he is your responsibility to kill.

timeline.summary: Hapatra resolves to find Bontu and Hazoret and keep them alive at all costs.
timeline.quote: We must find Bontu and Hazoret and keep them alive at all costs.

timeline.summary: Hazoret meets Samut and Djeru and orders them to protect others and hide until the God-Pharaoh comes, calling Djeru her final champion.
timeline.quote: And you, Djeru, my final champion.

timeline.summary: Samut asks who will protect Hazoret, who tells her to fight and says she will endure.
timeline.quote: Who will protect you , Hazoret?

timeline.summary: Samut leads a band of survivors toward the desert at Hazoret's command, guarded by Djeru.
timeline.quote: Hazoret's command burned at the back of Samut's thoughts as they moved.

timeline.summary: Samut tells the survivors that the God-Pharaoh is a lie and a trespasser, and Masikah doubts her.
timeline.quote: He is a trespasser, an interloper from another world.

timeline.summary: The survivors all feel the pain of a fourth god dying, and Samut tells them four gods are now dead.
timeline.quote: Four of our gods are now dead.

timeline.summary: Djeru publicly declares he stands with Samut against the God-Pharaoh.
timeline.quote: I have seen more than I needed to realize she speaks truth.

timeline.summary: Samut resolves to go back into the city to protect Hazoret, and Djeru and other warriors join her while Hapatra stays to guide the survivors into the sands.
timeline.quote: I am Rhonas's broken fang, and I know where to strike to stop the undead and the monstrosities in their tracks.

timeline.summary: Samut and Djeru fight the Eternal Neheb the Worthy and are beaten back.
timeline.quote: Neheb swung his spear forward, sending a wave of flame at Samut.

timeline.summary: Gideon blocks Neheb's spear and the Gatewatch destroy the Eternals; Samut stabs Neheb and kills him.
timeline.quote: She sprinted toward the Eternal minotaur and stabbed him in the back with both khopeshes

timeline.summary: The Gatewatch decide to bring the fight to Bolas, and Samut charges them to slay Nicol Bolas.
timeline.quote: Slay the dragon trespasser. Slay Nicol Bolas.

timeline.summary: Djeru persuades Samut to stand down and find the last god while the Gatewatch fight Bolas.
timeline.quote: Find the last god of Amonkhet, protect her, and protect the people of our city.

timeline.summary: Samut and Djeru, guided by the young vizier Haq, find Rhonas's body and Samut rallies the survivors.
timeline.quote: We will embody the strength Rhonas taught us

timeline.summary: A sandstorm sweeps in as an injured Hazoret emerges pursued by the scorpion god.
timeline.quote: A scorpion's tail pierced through the haze

timeline.summary: Samut leaps onto the scorpion god and cuts through its softened carapace while the survivors fight it.
timeline.quote: She smashed into the scorpion god's side, and her blades pierced its carapace

timeline.summary: Djeru trips the scorpion god and Samut redirects its fall so an obelisk pierces its chest.
timeline.quote: an earth-shattering crunch echoed across the battlefield as the obelisk pierced the scorpion god's chest.

timeline.summary: Hazoret thanks Samut, and Samut's planeswalker spark ignites; she is carried to another plane and returns to Amonkhet.
timeline.quote: she was falling, falling through space, through flashing waves of aether

timeline.summary: Samut realizes she is a walker between worlds and returns to Amonkhet, then collapses and is caught by Hazoret.
timeline.quote: I am a walker between worlds.

timeline.summary: Hazoret tells the survivors to endure and leads them into the desert as Bolas flies above, and Djeru and the survivors kneel to her.
timeline.quote: we must simply endure, persist, survive

timeline.summary: The Gruul, Izzet and Simic forces fight together, and the group meets planeswalkers Kiora and Samut, who frees dead Eternals by name.
timeline.quote: You are free, Eknet.

timeline.summary: Four God-Eternals emerge from the portal over Tenth District Plaza, and Samut identifies them as her plane's gods, now Bolas's servants.
timeline.quote: They are our gods,

timeline.summary: Jace lays out five problems: the Beacon, the Immortal Sun, the Planar Bridge, Liliana Vess, and Bolas himself.
timeline.quote: We face a number of problems. Five to be exact.

timeline.summary: Attendees argue about surrender or hiding, and Vorel blames planeswalkers while the archer and Samut insist Bolas is never sated.
timeline.quote: There is literally nothing left of my world, Skalla, thanks to him.

timeline.summary: Guild forces and planeswalkers charge the Citadel as the Dreadhorde engages them.
timeline.quote: Those Planeswalkers not fallen—or not yet fallen—were side by side with guild warriors, engaging the silent Dreadhorde.

timeline.summary: Chandra and Jaya burn the remaining Dreadhorde to ashes with dignity at Samut's request.
timeline.quote: meticulously burned every last one—every last fragment—down to ashes

timeline.summary: Across the Multiverse the worlds begin to overlay; on Ravnica, Bloomburrow, Amonkhet and Dominaria, people see doubles of their worlds.
timeline.quote: Meanwhile, the worlds begin to overlay.

timeline.summary: Samut is a leader among her crop, highly dependable in battle and seeming to be everywhere at once.
timeline.quote: She was a leader among her crop, and was highly dependable during battle.

this time piercing the base of its neck.

relations.quote: We must defy the great trespasser.

relations.note: She fights Eternals she once knew.
relations.quote: knew them I guess from when they were her friends.

relations.note: Close friends, unstoppable among the initiates.
relations.quote: She and her close friend Djeru were unstoppable among the initiates.

pages_say.description: A former member of the Tah crop and Djeru's closest friend who became a dissenter and was removed.
A fast, rash and curious girl of the Tah crop, Djeru and Nakht's friend, who later discovers that the God-Pharaoh is the Great Trespasser.
A fugitive dissenter and former initiate of the Tah crop who tries to keep her friend Djeru from dying in the final Trial.
A dissenter who stays at Djeru's side, doubts the God-Pharaoh, and draws her khopeshes at the demon.
A dissenter who joins Hapatra with Djeru to protect Oketra and tells her the gods were manipulated.
A dissenter with twin khopeshes who questions the God-Pharaoh and asks Hazoret who will protect her.
A dissenter with twin khopeshes who rallies Amonkhet's survivors against the God-Pharaoh and whose planeswalker spark ignites as she is thanked by Hazoret.
A young human planeswalker from Amonkhet who names the Eternals she kills, whom she once knew.
A planeswalker from Amonkhet who volunteers to go back through the portal and warns Bolas is never sated.
A planeswalker from Amonkhet whose world was devastated by Bolas.
A planeswalker who helped shut down the Planar Bridge.
A planeswalker from Amonkhet who beheads Eternals and asks for dignity for her people.
A planeswalker hiding with Hazoret and Amonkhet's population.
A resident of Amonkhet who shivers and looks to Hazoret for guidance.
A renowned initiate, master of the double khopesh and a dependable leader among her crop; she later became a planeswalker.
